battle.name: 北周統一北方
battle.brief: 五七二年起，北周在宇文邕親政之後與北齊在晉陽、平陽一線開戰，先取平陽，再兩路進逼，於汾水擊破齊軍；五七七年大軍東下，攻破鄴城，北齊後主出奔青州被斬，北方重歸一統。卡面的羅馬標槍早在數百年前退出歐洲軍中，此處只作對照。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 北周一方：五五七年宇文覺代西魏建周，都長安，疆域以關中為核心，兼有河西走廊、漢中、五五四年新取的益州，以及洛陽以南的部分郡縣，與北齊隔河、隔太行相望。軍隊以西魏府兵為底子，柱國與大將軍各領一軍，軍下設師、旅，兵皆編戶，平日耕織、有事則集；北周承襲其制，軍中的骨幹是漢人與鮮卑、羯、氐將領結成的關隴集團。宇文護以大冢宰秉政期間，軍國大權集中於相府；宇文邕殺宇文護之後，改由皇帝直領中外大都督，二十四軍分統於諸軍，軍令可以直達將校。馬政是周軍的命脈，關中與涼州出馬，騎兵按編制與步兵搭配，遠征時步騎並進。北齊一方：五五〇年高洋受魏禪建齊，都鄴，疆域包括河北、山東、豫北、晉南與河內，幅員與戶口遠勝北周；兵源眾多，軍中以鮮卑騎兵為精銳，漢人士兵填步卒與攻城之役，漢將與鮮卑將混編，軍令經尚書省與大將軍府下達，前線多以大將軍、柱國為統帥，鄴城另置京畿宿衛與城防系統。齊的內部有一道致命裂縫：和士開、祖珽等權臣與宮闈左右掌權，斛律光、高長恭等宿將只握兵柄而不得預政，朝廷內耗直接削弱了北齊的戰爭動員能力。此外柔然控弦漠北而附於北齊，北周則遣使結好突厥，從北面牽制；南面的陳朝自守，兩家都曾遣使往來，但陳朝並未介入北方的戰事。
countriesEn: The side of the Northern Zhou: in 557 Yuwen Jue replaced the Western Wei and founded the Zhou, with its capital at Chang'an. Its territory had its core in Guanzhong, and took in the corridor of Hexi, Hanzhong, the Shu region taken in 554, and a number of commanderies south of Luoyang; it faced the Northern Qi across the river and across the Taihang mountains. Its army was built on the fubing of the Western Wei: pillar lords and generals each commanded a division, the divisions were subdivided into corps and regiments, the soldiers were enrolled households who tilled and wove in time of peace and mustered in time of war; the Zhou inherited that system, and the backbone of the army was the group of Guanzhong lords and of Xianbei, Jie and Di commanders. While Yuwen Hu held the state as chancellor, the authority of war and government was concentrated in the office of the chancellor; after Yuwen Tai's brother had Yuwen Hu killed, the emperor himself took the command of the great commanders, the twenty-four divisions were allotted to the various armies, and the order of battle could reach the captains directly. The horse was the life of the Zhou army: Guanzhong and Liangzhou supplied the horses, and the cavalry was matched to the infantry in the establishment, horse and foot marching together on long campaigns. The side of the Northern Qi: in 550 Gao Yang received the abdication of the Wei and founded the Qi, with its capital at Ye. Its territory held Hebei, Shandong, northern Henan, southern Jin and Henei, and in extent and in registered households it far exceeded the Northern Zhou. Its manpower was large, the Xianbei horse were its picked troops, Han soldiers filled the foot and the work at the walls, Han and Xianbei commanders were mixed in the same units, and orders went down through the department of state affairs and the offices of the great generals, with the front usually commanded by a great general or a pillar lord, while the capital at Ye had its own capital guard and its own system of wall defence. The Qi had one fatal crack in its side: ministers such as He Shikai and Zu Ting, together with the palace, held the reins of power, while such old generals as Hulü Guang and Gao Changgong commanded troops but were kept out of the government; the friction at court told directly on the Qi capacity to mobilise for war. Beyond that, the Rouran held their bowstrings over the steppe and were attached to the Qi, while the Zhou sent envoys to court the Turks and so pincered from the north; the Chen in the south kept to itself, and the two exchanged envoys, but the Chen did not enter the fighting in the north.
people: 宇文邕（周武帝）是這場戰爭的推手。五六一年即位時年方十九，兄長宇文護以大冢宰身份專政，他名義上是天子，軍國大計卻都出於相府。他以漢人對付漢人權臣的手段取回權力：先在宮中殺死宇文護，盡罷其黨羽，收兵權於己手；再誅除宇文護之子宇文會、宇文顯等內亂分子，斷絕河北舊族在軍中的根。於是五七二年他才能以皇帝之尊調動關隴的全部人力物力去對付北齊，而不像先帝那樣被相府架空。統軍者是宇文氏宗室與關隴舊將：宇文憲（初名孝）為大軍主將，平陽、晉陽兩戰居功，滅齊後位大冢宰，卻與宇文護爭權，晚年被免官而終為所忌；尉遲迥、宇文雄、宇文昱、宇文邈、王軌各道併進，其中尉遲迥在北周與楊堅爭衡時起兵反抗，被王誼所平。楊堅在此只是配角：其女後被冊為中宮，他以車騎大將軍、尚書右僕射參預軍事與宮廷，是宇文邕晚年最信任的外戚。北齊的敗亡同樣出於人為：高緯（後主）性怯而好諂，和士開、祖珽相繼擅權，斛律光因不肯隨黨而被誅於晉陽，連其家屬亦不能保全；高長恭戰功赫赫卻因直言而失歡，段韶、尉長命等宿將屢請出戰而見疑。戰後北齊君臣被解送長安者以千計，高氏一族至此覆滅。
peopleEn: Yuwen Yong, Emperor Wu of the Zhou, was the man who drove this war. He was nineteen when he took the throne in 561, and his elder brother Yuwen Hu governed as chancellor, so that in name he was the emperor while every decision of war and government came out of the chancellor's office. He took back the power by using Han against Han ministers: first he had Yuwen Hu killed inside the palace, scattered his faction and gathered the command of the troops into his own hands; then he put to death such rebel sons of Yuwen Hu as Yuwen Hui and Yuwen Xian, cutting the root that the old Hebei families still had in the army. Only then, in 572, could he move the whole manpower and material of Guanzhong against the Northern Qi as emperor in his own right, instead of being set aside as his predecessors had been. The command was in the hands of the Yuwen clan and of the old generals of Guanzhong. Yuwen Xian, originally named Yuwen Xiao, was the chief general of the great army and earned his credit at Pingyang and at Jinyang; after the fall of the Qi he became chancellor in the highest rank, yet he fell out with Yuwen Hu, was removed from his post late in life and remained a man to be watched. Yuwen Xiong, Yuwen Yu, Yuwen Miao, Wang Gui and Yuwen Jiong advanced by separate routes, and it was Yuwen Jiong who later rose in arms against the Zhou when the Zhou and Yang Jian were struggling for power, and was put down by Wang Yi. Yang Jian was only a supporting actor in this: his daughter was later made a Zhou empress, and as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Chancellor of the department of state affairs he took part in the military and in the palace, and was the most trusted consort of Yuwen Yong in his last years. The fall of the Northern Qi was likewise made by men. Gao Wei, the Later Lord, was timid and given to flattery, and He Shikai and Zu Ting took turns to hold power; Hulü Guang was put to death at Jinyang because he would not go with the faction, and not even his family was spared; Gao Changgong, with great deeds to his name, lost the ruler's favour for speaking frankly, and such old generals as Duan Shao and Wei Changming asked again and again to be sent out and were doubted. After the war the officials of the Northern Qi were sent to Chang'an by the thousand, and the house of Gao was extinguished.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬標槍是公元前一百年前後羅馬共和末期軍中的投射兵器，槍幹中空、外套鐵箍，捅穿盾面之後槍桿即折，敵兵不能重新舉盾，只能拖著半截槍退回掩體。羅馬軍用它在前鋒齊射，射罷由輕裝步兵與重裝步兵接戰，騎兵負責追擊潰散之敵。到五七二年的中原，這件武器早已絕跡：共和末年的投槍在歐洲軍中歷數百年而被更輕的標矛與騎兵長矛取代，中原更不曾有過折斷槍桿以廢敵盾的設計；古籍中的「標」多指標箭，與拉丁語 pilum 所指的投槍並非一事。可以對照的是五七二至五七七年北方兩軍真正用得著的兵器：步軍結陣以槊、矛、戟與刀為主，長身大槊配鐵刃，柄用白木或柏木，與先秦以來槊不折的工藝取向一致；騎兵執大槊與環首刀，斜馳衝陣；投射武器以弓為主，臂弓、蹶張弓與車弩並用，車弩用來壓制城頭與密集隊形；攻城裝備有撞車、雲梯、攻城樓、鈎車與木魰雕，守方則備橫木、拒馬、鹿角、穿穴、甕火與水局；投石機用於遠距轟擊城頭與堤壩。遠征的補給靠牛車、櫂船與關中屯田，齊軍倚河北的水網與倉廩；這一條補給線的長短，往往比一次會戰更早決定戰局。
kitsEn: The Roman pilum on this card was the missile of the Roman army in the closing years of the Republic, around a hundred years before the Christian era. Its shaft was hollow and sleeved with iron, so that after it had punched through a shield the shaft broke off, and the enemy could not raise that shield again: he had to drag himself back behind cover with half a weapon still in his hand. The Romans fired it in files from the front, and when the volley was done the light infantry and then the heavy infantry took over the fight, while the horse hunted down and destroyed what had broken. By 572 the weapon was long extinct in the Central Plain: the throwing spear of the late Republic had been displaced in Europe over a period of several centuries by lighter javelins and by the lance of the cavalry, and the Central Plain had never had the design of breaking the shaft in order to make an enemy's shield useless. The character that the old Chinese texts use for the pilum, the biao, most often denotes a marked arrow, and is not the same thing at all as the throwing spear that the Latin pilum names. What can actually be set against the card is what the two northern armies of 572 to 577 really used. The foot formed up with the shuo, the spear, the halberd and the sabre, the long shuo with an iron blade, its shaft of white wood or cypress, following the Chinese craft principle established in the early ages that a shuo does not break. The cavalry carried the long shuo and the ring-pommel sabre and charged at an angle. Missiles were the bow above all, with the single-shot arm bow, the drawn crossbow and the waggon crossbow all in use, the waggon crossbow serving to pin the parapet and dense formations. The siege train included battering rams, ladders, siege towers, hooked poles and the wooden eagle, and the defenders equipped themselves with transverse beams, caltrops, antler barriers, counter-mines, fire pots and water-throwing devices; the stone-throwers served for long-range bombardment of parapets and of the dykes. Supply on a long march rested on ox carts, river craft and the land settlement of Guanzhong, while the Qi drew on the water network and the granaries of Hebei; the length of that supply line very often settled the outcome before a single pitched battle was fought.
tactics: 南北朝後期通行的戰爭樣式，是野會戰、攻城戰與邊境消耗戰三者交替。北周在關中修屯田、築城塢、置耕兵，使邊境不至空虛，出兵第一步便是以平陽為支點的攻取：周軍取平陽之後，北齊以大軍圍城，周軍閉城固守，倚城垣、井水與城內屯糧待援，不與敵人野戰；待援軍到、敵圍解，北齊主力在汾水一線與周軍遭遇，齊軍以騎兵密集衝擊，周軍以步兵結陣、弩手居中列抵禦，兩翼以騎兵反覆掠陣，齊軍終於退走。五七三至五七五年間，雙方在汾水、晉陽反覆拉鋸，齊軍名將斛律光、高長恭屢以精騎突破周軍的步兵陣地，周軍則以守城、斷糧與側翼迂迴相持，戰線由汾水逐步推向太行與滏口。五七七年秋，宇文邕集大軍東下，分道出師：西路取平陽、晉陽，中路直趨鄴城，東路自汲郡、黎陽一線渡河，斷齊軍歸路。攻鄴用雲梯、撞車與木魰雕並行，填壕、壓堞、覆穴三法同時進行；守方依城樓、射堞與甕火抵禦，糧道一斷，軍心先崩。齊主與妃嬪乘輕車自鄴出奔青州，周軍追之，青州城破，北齊覆亡。攻城與追擊首尾相連，是這一戰與此前四十餘年拉鋸最大的不同。
tacticsEn: The pattern of war in the late Southern and Northern Dynasties was the alternation of pitched battle, siege and the grinding attrition of the frontier. The Northern Zhou opened up land settlement in Guanzhong, raised walled farmsteads and posted farming troops, so that the border was never empty; and the first step of any campaign was to take a pivot such as Pingyang. After the Zhou took Pingyang, the Northern Qi closed in with a great army to besiege it, and the Zhou shut the gates, held the town and waited on the wall, on the wells and on the grain stored inside rather than giving battle in the open; when the relieving force came up and the siege lifted, the main body of the Qi met the Zhou on the line of the Fen river, the Qi horse charged in dense formation, the Zhou answered with infantry drawn up in array and crossbowmen in the centre, and the horse on both wings worked round the enemy again and again, until the Qi withdrew. Between 573 and 575 the two sides pulled at each other along the Fen and at Jinyang, the Qi commanders Hulü Guang and Gao Changgong breaking the Zhou foot with picked horse time and again, and the Zhou answering with siege, with cutting of supply and with flanking turns, so that the line of contact moved by degrees from the Fen river towards the Taihang and the Fu river. In the autumn of 577 Yuwen Yong gathered his great army and sent it east by several routes: the west road took Pingyang and Jinyang, the middle road drove straight for Ye, and the east road crossed the river at Ji commandery and at Liyang to cut the Qi's line of retreat. The assault on Ye used ladders, battering rams and the wooden eagle together, filling the ditch, pressing the parapet and filling in the breaches being carried out at the same time; the defenders answered with the towers, the loopholes and the fire pots of the wall, and once the supply road was cut the morale of the garrison broke before the walls did. The lord of Qi and his consorts left Ye in light carriages for Qingzhou, the Zhou army followed, the city of Qingzhou fell, and the Northern Qi was extinguished. That the siege and the pursuit were joined one to the other is the greatest difference between this war and the pulling and hauling of the preceding forty years.
data: 可以核對的錨點如下。時間：五五七年宇文覺代魏建北周；五六一年宇文邕即位，宇文護專政；五七一年十月宇文邕殺宇文護，五七二年春發兵攻齊，其餘黨宇文會、宇文顯等先後伏誅；五七三至五七五年間雙方在汾水、晉陽一線拉鋸；五七七年八月大舉東伐，圍鄴城，同年十月鄴城陷、北齊亡；五七八年八月宇文邕崩，宇文贇即位；五八一年楊堅代周建隋。疆域：北周據關中、河西、益州與漢中，北齊據河北、山東、豫北與晉南；北齊之富庶遠勝北周，這也是北周必須靠集中兵力與指揮取勝、不能靠消耗取勝的原因。兵員：諸史只給概數，北周北伐之師記為眾二十萬一類的圓數，齊軍在汾水與鄴城一線亦記為數十萬之眾，雙方實際可戰之卒多半遠低於宣稱的數目。城池：鄴城為北方第一大城，四面城垣周二十餘里，城內有銅雀、金虎、冰井、鐵虎四臺，漳水與滏水繞城；平陽、晉陽為關鍵支點，距鄴城各數百里。物資：遠征靠關中屯田與洛陽、黃河、漳水的水陸轉輸，軍中以粟麥為主，戰馬、弩機與甲械的耗損都極可觀。損失：齊軍在汾水與鄴城兩役皆大潰，俘降以萬計；《北齊書》與《周書》對斬首數字、俘虜總數與各役日期的記載互有出入，只採可互相印證的量級。戰役總跨度約五年，最後決戰集中在五七七年秋冬。
dataEn: The points that can be checked are as follows. Timing: in 557 Yuwen Jue replaced the Wei and founded the Northern Zhou; in 561 Yuwen Yong took the throne and Yuwen Hu governed; in October 571 Yuwen Yong had Yuwen Hu killed, and in the spring of 572 he sent his army against the Qi, the remaining faction of Yuwen Hu, men such as Yuwen Hui and Yuwen Xian, being put to death in turn; between 573 and 575 the two sides pulled at each other along the Fen and at Jinyang; in August 577 the great campaign east began, Ye was invested, and in October of the same year Ye fell and the Northern Qi was extinguished; in August 578 Yuwen Yong died and Yuwen Yun took the throne; in 581 Yang Jian replaced the Zhou and founded the Sui. Territory: the Zhou held Guanzhong, Hexi, Shu and Hanzhong, the Qi held Hebei, Shandong, northern Henan and southern Jin; the Qi was far richer than the Zhou, and for that very reason the Zhou had to win by concentration of troops and by command, and not by a war of exhaustion. Strength: the histories give only round figures; the Zhou army on the eastern campaign is given as a host of two hundred thousand in the round, and the Qi army on the Fen and before Ye likewise as tens of thousands of men, while the troops actually fit to fight on either side were certainly far fewer than the numbers claimed. Fortresses: Ye was the first great city of the north, its walls running more than twenty li round on four sides, with the platforms of Tongque, Jinhu, Bingjing and Tiehu inside it, and the Zhang and the Fu waters running past the town; Pingyang and Jinyang were the pivots, each of them several hundred li from Ye. Supply: the long march drew on the land settlement of Guanzhong and on the water and road transport of Luoyang, the Yellow River and the Zhang; the army lived on millet and wheat, and the wastage of horses, crossbow mechanisms and armour was very heavy. Losses: the Qi army broke up at the Fen and before Ye, and the prisoners and surrenders are counted by the tens of thousands; the Northern Qi History and the Zhou History differ over the numbers of heads taken, over the totals of prisoners and over the dates of the several actions, so only the order of magnitude that the two can confirm is used here. The campaign as a whole spans about five years, with the final decision concentrated in the autumn and winter of 577.
cause: 四層原因疊在一起。第一層是北周內部集權的完成：五五七年建國時，軍權全在宇文護一人之手，宇文護連廢立宇文邕都能干預，五七一年十月被殺之後，皇帝才第一次直接握住關隴的人、馬、甲兵與府兵，第二年才有條件把全部力量壓向北方。第二層是北齊的政變式腐敗：高緯在位時，宮闈與外朝都歸於和士開、祖珽等少數權臣，斛律光因不肯黨附而被誅，高長恭因直言而罷軍，宿將與朝廷互相猜忌，國家的機器在需要全面動員的時候反而轉不動。第三層是兩國資源結構的差異與各自的決策：北周地小而兵精，關隴集團有共同利害，府兵制使兵農合一，屯田使關中養得起遠征的糧；北齊地廣而兵多，卻要在內耗中把這些兵調出來。第四層是北方的地緣格局：柔然居漠北而附於北齊，北周結好突厥以為牽制；南面的陳朝自守，兩家都曾遣使，但陳朝介入北方用兵的可能性極低。於是這不是一場勢均力敵的消耗戰，而是北周以集權之利、選擇之專，集中五年的時間窗口，把北齊在內部損耗中失去的戰爭能力一次性兌現。
causeEn: Four layers of cause lie on top of one another. The first is the completion of the concentration of power inside the Northern Zhou. At the founding of the state in 557 all the military authority was in the hands of Yuwen Hu alone, to the point that he could set up and set aside Yuwen Yong as he wished; and only after his death in October 571 did the emperor hold the men, the horses, the armour and the fubing of Guanzhong in his own hand, so that only in the following year was he in a position to press the whole of that strength against the north. The second is the coup-like rot of the Northern Qi. While Gao Wei sat on the throne, both the inner palace and the outer court belonged to a few ministers such as He Shikai and Zu Ting; Hulü Guang was put to death for refusing to join a faction, Gao Changgong was relieved of his command for speaking frankly, and the old generals and the court distrusted one another, so that the machinery of the state could not be set moving at the very moment when a general mobilisation was required. The third is the difference in the structure of resources and in decision-making on each side. The Zhou was small in extent but its troops were good: the Guanzhong group had common interests, the fubing system joined soldier and farmer, and the land settlement let Guanzhong feed a long march; the Qi was wide and numerous, but it had to move those troops out of a country wasting itself in internal friction. The fourth is the geography of the north. The Rouran sat in the steppe and were attached to the Qi, and the Zhou courted the Turks to hold them in check; the Chen in the south kept to itself, and the two exchanged envoys, but the possibility of the Chen entering the northern war was very small. So this was not a war of exhaustion between even parties: it was the Zhou turning to account, with the advantage of concentrated power and the luxury of choosing its moment, a five-year window of time, and cashing in at one stroke the capacity for war that the Qi had lost to its own internal waste.
impact: 北方統一是這場戰爭最直接也最重的後果。五七七年之後，黃河兩岸不再有兩個互相攻殺的北朝政權，南北對峙的格局只剩下陳朝一方，隋文帝於五八九年滅陳，五八三年間的南北分立只維持了十二年。但統一帶來的制度並沒有留在宇文氏手上：宇文邕五七八年病死，宣帝宇文贇昏暴，權歸宇文護，楊堅於五八一年受禪代周建隋，北周辛苦打下來的北方，轉手就成了隋朝的家底。北周承襲的府兵與屯田、軍政編制、禮制與漢化政策，經隋入唐，成為唐代府兵制、均田制與三省制的底本；北朝末年以來關隴集團的婚姻與軍功網絡，也在此後數代通向唐室的關隴血統。北周崇儒而抑佛，五七四年建德三年下令斷佛道二教、毀經像、令沙門道士還民，這是北方佛教一次大的打擊，也延後了佛教在北方的再起。軍事技術上，圍攻城池的木鵓、撞車、雲梯與地下隧道攻防在這一輪戰爭中再度成熟，被後世兵書吸收。卡面那件羅馬標槍在此還有一層提醒：它提醒的是武器與制度的壽命差——一件共和末年的投槍在數百年裡退場，而北周留下的府兵與屯田，卻一路走進了唐代。
impactEn: The unification of the north is the most direct and the heaviest consequence of this war. After 577 there was no longer a pair of northern states tearing at each other on both banks of the Yellow River; the only side left in the north-south confrontation was the Chen, and the Sui emperor destroyed it in 589, so that the division of north and south lasted only the twelve years from 583. But the institutions that the unification brought were not left in the hands of the Yuwen: Yuwen Yong died of illness in 578, the Emperor Yuwen Yun who followed was dissolute and the power went to Yuwen Hu, and in 581 Yang Jian received the abdication and founded the Sui, so that the north that the Zhou had won by such labour became at one stroke the inheritance of the Sui. The fubing and the land settlement, the military administrative structure, the rites and the Sinicising policy that the Zhou inherited passed through the Sui into the Tang and became the base of the Tang fubing, of the equal-field system and of the three departments; and the web of marriage and military service that the Guanzhong group had woven since the end of the Northern Dynasties led, over the following generations, to the Guanzhong blood of the Tang house. The Zhou honoured the Confucian scholars and put down the Buddhists: in 574, in the third year of Jiande, the order went out to cut off the two teachings of Buddha and of Lao, to destroy the scriptures and the images and to send the monks and the Daoists back to ordinary life, which was a heavy blow to the Buddhism of the north and deferred the revival of the faith there. On the technical side, the wooden eagle, the battering ram, the ladder and the underground counter-tunnelling of the siege came to maturity again in this round of war and were taken up by the military writers of later ages. The Roman pilum on the card carries one further reminder: it points to the difference in the life of a weapon and the life of an institution. A throwing spear from the closing Republic left the field within a few hundred years, while the fubing and the land settlement left by the Northern Zhou walked all the way into the Tang.
result: 北齊亡。五七七年十月，鄴城被北周軍攻破，北齊後主高緯與妃嬪、幼主出奔青州，青州城破時高緯被周軍所殺，斛律氏與諸妃亦死於城中，北齊宗室與百官被解送長安；北齊的州郡、府庫、圖籍與部曲全歸北周，河北重鎮如晉陽、平陽自此在周軍控制之下，幽州方向的殘部在同年秋冬間陸續平定，記錄的月份兩書不一。北方由北周統一，疆域東至渤海，南至淮、漢中與巴蜀盡入版圖。對北齊的將領與官僚而言，降者多仍被授官，故土未嘗失；對北方百姓而言，二十餘年分裂之後第一次有一個政權能以同一套軍令、同一個朝廷號令從長安直達幽州。但戰後的北周並不寬鬆：宇文憲位大冢宰而與權臣宇文護相爭，晚遭猜忌；宇文邕一死，宣帝宇文贇昏暴，權歸宇文護，楊堅於五八一年受禪代周建隋。五七七年的北方一統，終究是以宇文氏的失位換來的。
resultEn: The Northern Qi was destroyed. In October 577 the city of Ye was taken by the Zhou army; Gao Wei, the Later Lord of Qi, with his consorts and his young son, fled to Qingzhou, and when the city of Qingzhou fell Gao Wei was killed by the Zhou soldiers, the Empress Hulü and the other consorts also died in the town, and the clan of Qi with its hundred officials was sent in bonds to Chang'an. The prefectures, the stores, the registers and the enrolled troops of the Qi all passed to the Zhou; the great strongholds of Hebei such as Jinyang and Pingyang were from that moment under Zhou control, and the rump that held out in the direction of Youzhou was put down in pieces in the autumn and winter of the same year, the months given for this differing between the two histories. The north was united by the Northern Zhou, whose territory now reached to the Bohai on the east and to the Huai, Hanzhong and Shu in the south. For the commanders and officials of the Qi, those who surrendered were mostly given office again, so that the land was not lost; for the people of the north, this was the first time in more than twenty years of division that a single government could issue its orders and its commands from Chang'an as far as Youzhou. But the Zhou after the victory was not at ease. Yuwen Xian became chancellor of the highest rank and fell out with the powerful minister Yuwen Hu, and was distrusted to the end; after Yuwen Yong's death the dissolute Emperor Yuwen Yun let the power go to Yuwen Hu, and in 581 Yang Jian received the abdication and founded the Sui. The unification of the north in 577 was in the end bought with the loss of the Yuwen house.
